speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've been treated for acute sinusitis recently. Can you describe the nature of your flank pain and confirm if you have noticed any changes in your urination, such as frequency or burning?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any burning or urgency when you urinate, and have you noticed any blood in your urine? I also need to know if you have a history of kidney stones or diabetes.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash following amoxicillin suggests a possible allergic interstitial nephritis, especially given the persistence of fever and flank pain. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_Microscopy_and_Culture

text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial Culture: Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in the urine strongly supports a diagnosis of acute interstitial nephritis triggered by your recent antibiotic therapy. I will now review any available renal imaging to assess kidney structure and rule out obstruction. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of dysuria and negative bacterial culture further rules out a typical urinary tract infection. Given the eosinophiluria, fever, and recent antibiotic exposure, the clinical picture is consistent with allergic interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
